newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia lashes US on Iraq as "bull in a china shop".
newsitem.headline: Russia lashes US on Iraq as "bull in a china shop".

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said on Thursday Washington was behaving like a "bull in a china shop" with its air strikes against Iraq, amid conflicting reports about whether Moscow was warned in advance.
"There is one big strong master (in the world) who spits on everybody," Interfax news agency quoted Lebed as saying.
"That master is behaving like a bull in a china shop," it said Lebed had told journalists during his latest peace mission to the rebel Russian region of Chechnya.
With characteristic cynicism, the growling former paratroop general went on to say that U.S. President Bill Clinton had carried out the attacks to boost his democratic image.
"This is the essence of true democracy -- carry out air raids and then gather the journalists to applaud," Lebed said.

Lebed's salvo was the latest of a series of Russian denunciations of the air strikes, launched by Washington against Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday in retaliation for Baghdad's military operation against separatist Kurds in the north.
On Thursday President Boris Yeltsin interrupted his holiday for a television interview in which he said he backed the government's opposition to the strikes.
"I approved the government statement protesting against that kind of unilateral action," he said in the interview, in which he also announced that he was to have heart surgery.
The government issued two statements this week, saying the strikes were unacceptable and demanding a halt to all military action against Iraq.
The first, on Tuesday, was followed by a second wave of strikes, a vivid demonstration of Moscow's lack of influence in world affairs since the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991.
Russian ultranationalist Vladimir Zhirinovsky taunted Yeltsin for not fighting against what he called U.S. banditry and said Clinton was "worse than Hitler".

"Napoleon and Hitler are children compared with Clinton. Clinton is worse than Hitler. The U.S. action is bullying on a planetary scale," Zhirinovsky said, calling on Russian pilots to fly to the defence of his friend, Iraqi leader Saddamm Hussein.
Yeltsin's foreign affairs adviser Dmitry Ryurikov told a news briefing that Russia's leadership had not even been informed of the U.S. plans in advance.
"To talk about coordination is simply not serious...The Russian leadership was not informed," Ryurikov said.
But Yeltsin's chief of staff Anatoly Chubais had earlier indicated that Russia had been consulted on Monday, the day before the first wave of strikes.
"To raise the question that such a scale of events could have occurred without consultations with Russia is simply irresponsible," Chubais said on Wednesday.

Two deputy foreign ministers, one of whom had been in Iraq just before the strikes, appeared to explain the contradiction when they told a news briefing Moscow had been warned of U.S. action in Iraq but not specifically notified of the strikes.

Russia has generally taken a softer line on Iraq than the United States since the end of the Gulf conflict, and has been pushing Washington and its Western European allies to lift crippling post-war sanctions against Baghdad.

Moscow fears the latest crisis could hurt its chances of recouping Baghdad's massive debt to the former Soviet Union because it is delaying a United Nations agreement to let sanction-squeezed Iraq sell some oil.
Yeltsin said he would discuss events in Iraq during talks planned for Saturday near Moscow with visiting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl. The visit was arranged before the latest crisis.
